exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Hong Kong Tower, Cathay two five one, runway vacated via Alpha fow-er.
exchanges.meaning: Reports the runway vacated via taxiway Alpha 4.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, Hong Kong Tower, roger, contact Ground wun two wun day-see-mal six.
exchanges.meaning: Acknowledges the vacated report and instructs the aircraft to contact Ground on 121.6.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Ground wun two wun day-see-mal six, Cathay two five one.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Hong Kong Ground, Cathay two five one, vacated Runway zero sev-en left at Alpha fow-er, request taxi to gate.
exchanges.meaning: Reports vacated Runway 07L at Alpha 4 and requests taxi to the gate.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, Hong Kong Ground, taxi to Stand November two fow-er via taxiway Golf, hold short of taxiway Bravo.
exchanges.meaning: Clears the aircraft to taxi to Stand N24 via taxiway Golf, holding short of taxiway Bravo.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Taxi to Stand November two fow-er via Golf, hold short of taxiway Bravo, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Readback of the taxi clearance to Stand N24 via Golf with the hold-short of Bravo.

vocabulary.definition: Instruction to exit active runway at specified turnoff.
Conditional frequency transfer upon completely clearing runway.
Report that all parts of the aircraft have crossed holding line.
Angled taxiway (30°) allowing turnoff at up to 50 knots.
Automated laser apron docking system (e.g. Safedock).

quiz.question: Under ICAO Annex 14 standards, when is an aircraft considered to have completely vacated an active runway?
options: When the nose landing gear crosses the runway edge line.
When all parts of the aircraft, including the tail, have completely crossed the runway holding position marking.
When the pilot applies reverse thrust.
When the aircraft slows below 30 knots.
quiz.explanation: An aircraft is not clear of the runway until all parts (fuselage, wings, and tail overhang) have completely passed the runway holding position marking.

quiz.question: What is the maximum recommended turnoff speed for an aircraft exiting a runway onto a standard ICAO Rapid-Exit Taxiway (RET) under dry conditions?
quiz.explanation: Under ICAO aerodrome design criteria, Rapid-Exit Taxiways for Code 3 and 4 runways are designed for turnoff speeds of up to 50 knots (93 km/h) under dry conditions.

sections.heading: Section 2: Core Learning Content & Vocabulary Table
sections.body: Vacate via [taxiway] — Instruction to exit active runway at specified turnoff. "Vacate left via Alpha four." / When vacated, contact Ground — Conditional frequency transfer upon completely clearing runway. Never switch while rolling on runway! / Runway vacated — Report that all parts of the aircraft have crossed holding line. Includes tail overhang past markings. / Rapid-Exit Taxiway (RET) — Angled taxiway (30°) allowing turnoff at up to 50 knots. Minimizes runway occupancy time. / Visual Docking Guidance (VDGS) — Automated laser apron docking system (e.g. Safedock). Guides aircraft to stop mark at gate.

sections.heading: Section 8: Spaced Repetition Review Drill
sections.body: Day 39 Review (+1d): In a go-around, apply TOGA thrust, pitch to 15°, retract flaps by one stage, and call "Positive rate, gear up". Standard missed approach climb gradient is 2.5%. / Day 33 Review (+7d): RNP approaches require on-board performance monitoring. Any RAIM failure past the FAF mandates an immediate missed approach. / Day 7 Review (+33d): Never cross an illuminated red stop-bar. Stop-bars protect runway safety areas against incursions.

sections.heading: Section 9: Fun Aviation Fact — The 50-Knot Turnoff
sections.body: Before the 1960s, runways only had 90-degree right-angle exits. Airliners had to brake down to 10 knots on the runway before turning, keeping the runway occupied for nearly 90 seconds! The invention of the Rapid-Exit Taxiway (RET) with a gentle 30-degree curved geometry allowed jets to exit at up to 50 knots (93 km/h), slashing Runway Occupancy Time down to 42 seconds and effectively doubling runway capacity worldwide!
